name: Ergometrine
aliases: ergonovine, Ergonovine, D-lysergic acid-L-propanolamide, ergobasine, Ergobasine, Ergometrina, Ergométrine, Ergometrinum
summary: Ergonovine, also known as ergometrine and lysergic acid propanolamide, is a medication used to cause contractions of the uterus to treat heavy vaginal bleeding after childbirth. It can be used either by mouth, by injection into a muscle, or injection into a vein.

pharmacology.text: Ergonovine stimulates the uterus and other smooth muscles. It targets α-adrenergic, dopaminergic, and serotonin receptors (the 5-HT2 receptor). Its uterotonic effect has not been identified with a specific receptor type. The drug has been found to bind to and activate the rat and human serotonin 5-HT2A receptor with similar affinity as lysergic acid diethylamide (LSD).
pharmacology.kind: Serotonin receptor agonist; Serotonin 5-HT2A receptor agonist; Uterotonic; Serotonergic psychedelic; Hallucinogen

uses.text: Ergonovine, also known as ergometrine and lysergic acid propanolamide, is a medication used to cause contractions of the uterus to treat heavy vaginal bleeding after childbirth. It can be used either by mouth, by injection into a muscle, or injection into a vein. It is on the World Health Organization's List of Essential Medicines.

sideEffects.text: Common side effects include high blood pressure, vomiting, seizures, headache, and low blood pressure.
